newsitem.title: CHINA: China rubber market in oversupply, prices suffer.
newsitem.headline: China rubber market in oversupply, prices suffer.

text.p: Rubber prices in China have fluctuated wildly in the past week, first being dragged down by low spot prices and then pushed up as big producers took the chance to speculate at low levels, traders said.
The price of the key June 1997 contract on the Hainan Futures Exchange fell 7.43 percent last week to end at 9,780 yuan($1,178) per tonne on Friday, traders said.
Prices rallied on Monday to close at 10,070 yuan per tonne, the trading sources in Hainan and Shanghai said.
"Over-supply of spot rubber depressed prices on the spot market, which dampened the futures market, and resulted in last weeks falls," a rubber futures trader in Shanghai said.
"After the futures price fell to lower than the spot price, rubber producers began to buy on the futures market, pushing prices up sharply today," he said.
"Whether they cash in the contracts or offset them on the futures market, they are sure to gain," he said.
Traders said the price of physical rubber is around 9,900 yuan per tonne in China's major production area of Hainan a tropical island province off China's southern coast.
Traders and industry officials said they could see no resolution to the over-supply situation in 1997 because imports are on the rise and domestic output looks healthy.

China's imports of natural rubber in the first four months of 1997 reached 156,301 tonnes, an increase of 15.5 percent over the same period last year, a trading source on the Hainan exchange told Reuters.
In April, imports surged 47.77 percent over March imports to 47,574 tonnes, against the figure in March, he said, quoting official figures.
"Supply is greatly in excess of demand," said an official with China's biggest natural rubber producer, Hainan Nongkeng (Group) Co.
"We may have a difficult situation this year despite signs of good output," he said.
The company's output this year is likely to reach a record 200,000 tonnes given favourable weather conditions, he said.
"China's total consumption of natural rubber usually totals 750,000 to 780,000 tonnes a year, with around 400,000 tonnes domestically produced and the rest being imported," he said.
"But because our customers have no cash, many rubber products makers cannot reach full capacity and are unable to buy much in the way of raw material," the official said.
He said rubber that was effectively smuggled from other producing countries in Southeast Asia to avoid import duties and value-added tax was compounding problems for Chinese producers.
"A lot of natural rubber comes into China through channels that enable importers to avoid taxes and this seriously affects our interests because it can be sold at lower-than-market prices," he said.
According to figures provided by futures traders, China had 200,000 tonnes of rubber in stock at the end of 1996.
A recent report from the official Xinhua news agency said China is negotiating with Thailand on a deal to import 500,000 tonnes rubber in 1997.
